derived_mir.markers_exact_is_vacuous_here: VACUOUS HERE, and the fixture says so rather than letting the word carry weight it has not earned: `markers_detail` is "0 marker line(s) identical", i.e. there are ZERO marker lines on either side, so `markers_exact: true` is a comparison of two empty sequences. Measured at this HEAD: 1055 of the 1072 A0 candidates are in that same zero-marker position; only 17 have any marker lines at all. This is NOT the same predicate `level::Level::is_zero` fails — that body has real markers that genuinely differ (its `markers_detail` carries an actual diff), so it fails NON-vacuously. A gate reading `markers_exact` as evidence of marker agreement is reading a vacuous truth for almost every candidate. DISCHARGED (partially, and only in the direction that was in doubt) by markers_channel_witness.json, measured from THIS SAME coverage dump: the channel compares 8 real marker lines and agrees on `flat::types::FlatFlags::contains` (which flips), and reports FALSE on `level::Level::is_zero`, whose markers genuinely differ and which the -O gate therefore refuses. So a zero-marker reading here is a fact about THIS body, not an artefact of a dead instrument. It still does NOT mean this body's markers were checked and agree.

bodyful_reachable_closure: PASS — the body makes NO calls (resolved 0, extern_decls 0, unresolved 0), so the reachable callee closure is the body itself and contains no declaration-only entry. This is the A0 criterion that FAILS for level::Level::is_zero, whose closure reaches Option::as_deref / Option::expect. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-13: still 0/0/0, so the criterion still holds, and is_zero still fails it (6 resolved calls at this HEAD, markers_exact false).

supersedes.why: Trust commit a59c2960bc, "fix(lineage): bind body digest to stable definition identity" (2026-08-11 18:37), bound each per-body lineage digest to that body's stable DefPathHash and bumped the domain constant `trust_thir_lower.body_lineage.v1` -> `v2`, exactly as that constant's own doc requires. It moved 12,440 of 13,068 per-body digests (95%) while every EMITTED IR body stayed byte-identical.
supersedes.what_this_is_not: This was a DOCUMENTED, CORRECTLY-VERSIONED scheme change. It is NOT a silent change, NOT a bug, and NOT evidence that any compiler code or any emitted body changed. The old digest is not wrong-for-its-time; it is a v1 name for a compiler that no longer exists, and a v1 name has no meaning under v2.
supersedes.why_the_gate_did_not_notice: crystal_a1_lineage.rs (and crystal_a1_lineage/level_kind_ord.rs) RECORD the digest rather than recompute it — they cannot recompute it, because re-deriving a body lineage requires running the trust compiler, which is not a dependency of this test. The gate therefore checks only the fixture's INTERNAL consistency: that `lineage` equals `flip_event.lineage`, that the raw event text carries the same string, and that the A0 booleans read as claimed. A globally stale-but-self-consistent fixture passes it. Re-pinning is a MANUAL obligation triggered by a trust-side domain bump, which is why `lineage_domain` is now recorded at top level.
supersedes.old_fixture_domain_label_was_not_evidenc: The superseded fixture already carried `trustc.lineage_domain = trust_thir_lower.body_lineage.v2` while pinning a digest minted by the pre-bump driver stamped (94147b34f 2026-08-11). Nothing in the repo cross-checked the label against the digest, so the label tracked intent rather than the driver actually used. Treat the pairing of `lineage` and `lineage_domain` as sound only when both come from the same recorded build.
